reasoning_content:
Interesting. Direct match_all works, but the proxy's match_all fails. However, match query ({"match":{"name":"Blinding Lights"}}) works via proxy and returns 1 hit.

So the proxy is forwarding the body. Let me think about why match_all fails via the proxy but match works.

The difference: `{"size":1,"query":{"match_all":{}}}` vs `{"size":1,"query":{"match":{"name":"Blinding Lights"}}}`.

Wait a sec. When PHP does json_decode and json_encode on `{"match_all":{}}`, PHP converts `{}` (empty object) into `[]` (empty array)! That's the bug. PHP's json_decode by default turns empty JSON objects into empty arrays. So `match_all:{}` becomes `match_all:[]`. And ES rejects `match_all:[]`.

But `{"match":{"name":"Blinding Lights"}}` has a non-empty object, so it's preserved. That's why match works but match_all fails.

This is a PHP quirk, and it affects `match_all:{}` (which the app may or may not use). This is a real but minor limitation of the shipped PHP proxy — it can't correctly pass through empty JSON objects. This only affects match_all queries.
